corrections.summary: Answer key changed C -> A. 'Start where you are' asks for objective observation, e.g. people with no prior knowledge of the service ('fresh eyes'). Same question as printed #105 (key A); this copy then becomes an identical duplicate.
Option C was printed as a second 'Warranty'; replaced by 'User experience', the fourth of the book's four concepts (utility, warranty, user experience, sustainability).
Truncated option 'Product Vend' completed as 'Product Vendor' (the book's digital product vendor role).
Removed the stray editorial line 'Add answer: D. The external partner providing technology.'; key C (sponsor authorizes the budget) confirmed.
ITIL 4 term 'service value system' renamed to the Version 5 term 'ITIL Value System'.
ITIL 4 term 'Service Value System' renamed to the Version 5 term 'ITIL Value System'.
ITIL 4 term 'Service Value System' renamed to the Version 5 term 'ITIL Value System'. Inputs (opportunity and demand) confirmed.
ITIL 4 term 'Service Value System' renamed to the Version 5 term 'ITIL Value System'. Outcome (value) confirmed.
ITIL 4 term 'dimension of service management' renamed to the Version 5 term 'dimension of product and service management'.

Answer key changed A -> B. The book places handling complexity through experimentation (probe, sense, respond) in the 'value streams and processes' dimension. Medium confidence: the book does not use the exact words 'safe-to-fail'.
Answer key changed A -> B, as for printed #93 (same question).
Answer key changed D -> C (owner decision). The book describes projects as time-bound initiatives that introduce new or changed products and services; the dump keys the same question C twice.
Answer key changed D (Operate) -> B (Support). In the book, incident resolution belongs to the 'support' activity.
ITIL 4 term 'dimension of service management' renamed to the Version 5 term 'dimension of product and service management'.

classificationMethod: Each occurrence was read by the auditor and mapped to one v5.0 assessment criterion. Bloom level defaults to the criterion's BL column; overrides are listed with a note. Classification is metadata only and never edits source text.
duplicateMethod: Stems normalised by NFKC, lower-casing, quote unification and removal of non-alphanumerics; identical normalised stems form a duplicate group. Near-duplicates (difflib ratio >= 0.85 AND correct-option text similarity >= 0.9) are merged into exclusion groups used only to prevent repeats within one exam.
